A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CD-T and its use for circuit discovery, despite substantial changes to the title, method and experiments. Both main texts and complete appendices are readable, and their equations, tables and figures support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original pathology circuit experiments, phrase-attribution results and an eleven-participant human study, including Tables 1–5 and Figure 2.

after.justification: V2 reports original CD-T evaluations on IOI, Greater-than and Docstring, including benchmark curves in Figures 1–2 and circuit analyses and numerical results in Appendix A.

M1.justification: V1 decomposes attention values while explicitly leaving attention weights undecomposed. V2 decomposes queries, keys, attention probabilities and outputs (Eqs. 6–15). Circuit discovery also replaces fixed top-N selection with revised relevance scoring, layer normalization, heuristic selection, pruning and performance-based stopping. V1's word2vec/PCA/k-means circuit-interpretation pipeline is removed.

E1.justification: The pathology/Gleason classification, SST-2 sentiment and AGNews topic experiments disappear, including their human evaluation. V2 instead evaluates indirect object identification, numerical Greater-than completion and Python Docstring completion. This replaces clinical and local-explanation coverage with language/code circuit-discovery tasks.

E2.justification: V1 evaluates path patching for circuit discovery and LIME, SHAP and Integrated Gradients in human experiments. V2 replaces these comparisons with ACDC optimized for KL divergence, EAP and manual-circuit references; random circuits remain comparators. ACDC participates in Figure 1 but is explicitly excluded from Figure 2. EAP-IG is discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: BERT-based experiments are replaced by GPT2-small and attn-only-4l protocols. V2 uses separate circuit-discovery and evaluation samples, task-specific corrupted inputs, and correctly answered examples only for Docstring. It introduces manual-circuit ROC-AUC sweeps over selection percentiles 90–99 and coarse-node comparisons. Faithfulness changes from v1's average true-class logit ratio to baseline-adjusted differences of dataset-average task scores.

E4.justification: V1's pathology word-cluster analyses, phrase-attribution cases and reported sensitivity to N are removed. V2 adds mean-versus-zero ablation comparisons, faithfulness-versus-circuit-size analyses and comparisons against random circuits of varying sizes. Appendix A adds IOI relevance heatmaps examining negative, backup and other functional heads, including disagreements with the manual analysis.

E5.justification: V1 averages random-baseline faithfulness over ten random seeds. V2 introduces a reference-distribution analysis estimating the probability that CD-T circuits are more faithful than random circuits across sizes, framed as circuit hypothesis testing (Section 5.2.2). It reports ten repetitions without confidence intervals. This changes the statistical procedure; it does not establish an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: V1's pathology results, including 46.0% versus 41.9% faithfulness, and its phrase/human-study findings disappear. V2 reports approximately 97% average manual-circuit ROC AUC, new runtime and size–faithfulness curves, and appendix results such as Docstring CD-T task score 3.235 and correct-guess rate 0.57. These are results under replacement tasks and protocols, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The attention decomposition is mathematically revised from fixed-weight value sums to decompositions through attention products and softmax. The relevance functional changes from average absolute relevant activation in v1 Eq. 1 to summed relevant/irrelevant L1-norm ratios in v2 Eq. 16. V2 also formalizes tasks and changes the mathematical definition of faithfulness. These are substantive definitions and equations, although no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from versatile local/mechanistic interpretation with clinical and human-study benefits to automated, fine-grained circuit discovery. V1's twofold speedup over path patching and user-trust claims are replaced by claims about recovery of manual circuits, hours-to-seconds runtime relative to ACDC, performance against random circuits and matching full-model faithfulness with fewer nodes.

C2.justification: Clinical hierarchy and human-trust interpretations are removed. V2 explains negative/supporting heads and ablation effects, and explicitly describes CD-T as combining direct and indirect effects rather than isolating direct effects. New limitations concern relevance-score scale and sign, heuristic tuning and limited human-understandable interpretation. Appendix A also qualifies the Greater-than reference comparison because all MLPs are retained.

D1.justification: V1's fine-tuning recipe, anonymized clinical examples and survey instructions are replaced by pretrained-model identifiers, corrupted-input distributions and explicit circuit/reference head lists. V2 specifies A100 hardware for its experiments. The code-access statement changes from code available in supplementary material to a promised future Python package; actual availability cannot be verified from the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: The local-attribution-centered review is substantially replaced by discussion of causal patching and automated circuit discovery. New positioning covers ACDC, EAP/EAP-IG, sparse-autoencoder methods and circuit hypothesis testing, including Conmy, Syed, Hanna, Marks, O'Neill and Shi. CD-T is now positioned primarily against approximation, training and granularity limitations of circuit-discovery methods.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, method exposition and conclusions are extensively rewritten around automated circuit discovery. V2 adds a standalone definitions section, reorganizes the methodological explanation and replaces the multipurpose appendix with task-specific experimental documentation. The title and author list also change.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. Pathology circuit/word-cluster diagrams, phrase tables, survey bars and attribution visualizations are replaced by runtime–ROC and random-circuit plots, three faithfulness curves, appendix relevance heatmaps and task-result tables. Algorithm 1 is also substantially reformatted to display the revised procedure.

improvement.justification: Standard-task comparisons, automated baselines, size curves and ablations strengthen v1's narrow circuit-discovery validation. The net gain is tempered by lost clinical/human coverage and the change from supplementary-code availability to a future release promise. New reporting problems also limit confidence: q*=0.8 is described as '80% more faithful,' while Appendix A.1.2 reports an ablated Greater-than score of -2.095 despite defining a probability-difference metric bounded by -1 and 1.
